overview: This Senate resolution supports naming September 13 through 19, 2026, as "National Adult Education and Family Literacy Week." It cites survey data showing that many U.S. adults have low reading or math skills, lack a high school diploma, or have limited English. It recognizes adult education, including literacy, math, English-language, digital and job-readiness classes, as an important part of the nation's education and workforce system. It encourages partnerships among adult education providers, employers, colleges and community groups and calls for expanding access to these programs. It does not provide funding. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 23, 2026.
for: Supporters say helping adults build basic reading, math and job skills strengthens families and the workforce, and the resolution draws attention to programs that make that possible.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not provide any new money for adult education programs.
